pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: 5+ symptoms during same 2-week period including depressed mood or anhedonia (DSM-5-TR).
ruleOuts: Bipolar disorder (run MDQ / rule out hypomania)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: CBT (Cognitive Restructuring), Behavioral Activation (BA), or Interpersonal Psychotherapy (IPT). In mild depression, psychotherapy alone is first-line; in moderate-to-severe, combined pharmacotherapy + CBT yields superior recovery rates.

firstLine.rationale: High tolerability, predictable kinetics, minimal CYP450 drug-drug interactions. Excellent for comorbid anxiety.
Gold standard in cardiac patients (SADHART trial); mild activating dopaminergic tone at >=100mg.
Zero sexual side effects, weight-neutral or mild weight loss, energizing noradrenergic/dopaminergic tone. (Contraindicated in seizure disorders or bulimia/anorexia).

secondLine.rationale: Dual 5-HT and NE reuptake inhibition (SNRI). Superior when physical fatigue, psychomotor retardation, or chronic pain/fibromyalgia co-exists.
NaSSA antagonist (alpha-2, 5-HT2A/C, 5-HT3, H1). Restores deep sleep architecture and stimulates appetite. Ideal for insomnia and unintended weight loss.
Multimodal serotonergic modulator with documented procognitive benefits for executive dysfunction and residual brain fog.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Addresses residual anhedonia, fatigue, and reverses SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction (W-Wellbutrin synergy).
FDA-approved partial dopamine agonist augmentation for treatment-resistant major depression.
Level 1 evidence for treatment-resistant depression and documented independent anti-suicide effect.
Rapid synaptogenic NMDA receptor antagonism for acute suicidal ideation or failed >=2 medication trials.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Bipolar I: At least 1 lifetime manic episode (>= 7 days or requiring hospitalization). Bipolar II: At least 1 hypomanic episode (>= 4 days) + 1 major depressive episode; no lifetime mania.
ruleOuts: Borderline personality disorder (affective instability lasts hours, not days/weeks)
ADHD (chronic baseline distractibility vs episodic mood elevation)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Social Rhythm Therapy (IPSRT) to stabilize circadian rhythms, Family-Focused Therapy (FFT), and CBT for bipolar disorder. Mandatory warning: Antidepressant monotherapy is strictly contraindicated due to manic switch and rapid-cycling risk.

firstLine.rationale: Gold-standard mood stabilizer for classic euphoric mania and maintenance. Proven neuroprotective and independent suicide-reduction efficacy.
First-line monotherapy approved across both acute mania and acute bipolar depression via active metabolite norquetiapine.
Superior for preventing and treating bipolar depression. Requires slow bi-weekly titration to prevent Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS).
FDA-approved for bipolar I depression. Low metabolic risk profile; take Latuda with >=350 calories.

secondLine.rationale: Preferred over lithium for dysphoric/mixed mania and rapid cycling. Monitor CBC, LFTs, and teratogenic risk in childbearing potential.
Rapid antimanic control with minimal metabolic weight gain.
FDA-approved for treatment-resistant bipolar depression. High metabolic vigilance required.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Dual mood stabilizer coverage for severe refractory mania or rapid cycling.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Mood Stabilizer (Lithium or Depakote) + SGA (Quetiapine / Aripiprazole)
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Standard of care for breakthrough manic episodes or severe psychotic features.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: >= 2 characteristic psychotic symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, grossly disorganized behavior, negative symptoms) active for >= 1 month, with total disturbance >= 6 months.
ruleOuts: Schizoaffective disorder (evaluate prominent mood episode timeline)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Psychosis (CBTp), Social Skills Training (SST), and Coordinated Specialty Care (CSC) for first-episode psychosis. Involve assertive community treatment (ACT) if adherence is compromised.

firstLine.rationale: Second-generation partial D2/D3 agonists. Low risk of metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, and sedation. Preferred for first-episode psychosis.

firstLine.agent: Risperidone (2–6mg) / Paliperidone (3–12mg or Invega Sustenna LAI)
firstLine.rationale: High D2 potency providing robust positive symptom resolution. Consider Long-Acting Injectable (LAI) early to prevent non-adherence and relapse.
Favorable metabolic profile; potent 5-HT7 antagonism improves cognitive functioning. Take with >=350 calories.

secondLine.rationale: Potent 5-HT2A/D2 antagonists with strong sedation and agitation control. High risk of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and dyslipidemia.

secondLine.agent: Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics (LAIs: Invega Sustenna/Trinza, Aristada, Abilify Maintena)
secondLine.rationale: Indicated after establishing oral tolerability to ensure relapse-free maintenance and bypass oral non-compliance.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: MANDATORY STEP 3: Indicated after failure of 2 adequate trials of different antipsychotics (at least 1 SGA). Gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and persistent suicidality. Requires ANC monitoring via REMS.
Advisable for persistent affective instability, impulsive hostility, or behavioral agitation.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Uninterrupted period of illness with a major mood episode (depressive or manic) concurrent with schizophrenia Criterion A, PLUS >= 2 weeks of delusions or hallucinations in the absence of a major mood episode.
ruleOuts: Bipolar disorder with psychotic features (psychosis occurs ONLY during mood episodes)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Psychoeducation regarding medication adherence, CBT for psychosis, and family-focused supportive therapy.

firstLine.rationale: The ONLY monotherapy specifically FDA-approved for Schizoaffective Disorder (both bipolar and depressive types).

firstLine.agent: Atypical Antipsychotic + Mood Stabilizer (Quetiapine / Risperidone + Lithium or Depakote) — *Bipolar Type*
firstLine.rationale: Dual coverage to suppress psychotic delusions while stabilizing manic/hypomanic polarity shifts.

firstLine.agent: Atypical Antipsychotic + SSRI/SNRI (Aripiprazole / Lurasidone + Sertraline / Escitalopram) — *Depressive Type*
firstLine.rationale: Targeted combination treating core psychotic features without destabilizing mood.

secondLine.rationale: High efficacy for refractory schizoaffective disorder with persistent mood and psychotic instability.

secondLine.agent: Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotic (LAI) + Oral Mood Stabilizer
secondLine.rationale: Stabilizes baseline psychosis and reduces hospitalization frequency in outpatient settings.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: High-yield evidence for intractable schizoaffective episodes, catatonia, or life-threatening depressive exhaustion.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Presence of 1+ delusions of at least 1 month's duration; functioning is not markedly impaired and behavior is not obviously bizarre outside the delusion; schizophrenia Criterion A is not met.
ruleOuts: Paranoid personality disorder (pervasive trait vs encapsulated fixed delusion)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) adopting a collaborative, non-confrontational stance. Crucial clinical rule: Never directly challenge or validate the delusion; explore the distress and anxiety caused by the beliefs.

firstLine.rationale: Modest D2 blockade to reduce delusional conviction and hyper-vigilant paranoia without severe side effects.

firstLine.agent: Pimozide (Orap 2–6mg) — *Historically preferred for Somatosensory / Monodelusional Paranoia*
firstLine.rationale: High affinity D2/opiate antagonist historically cited for somatic delusions (e.g. delusional parasitosis), requiring baseline ECG/QTc surveillance.

secondLine.rationale: Stronger sedative properties beneficial when delusions generate severe agitation, insomnia, or confrontational behavioral discord.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Addresses secondary depressive demoralization, social withdrawal, or comorbid obsessional anxiety.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Excessive anxiety and worry occurring more days than not for at least 6 months across multiple events, with >= 3 somatic symptoms (restlessness, fatigue, concentration, muscle tension, sleep).
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: CBT (identifying worry loops, cognitive restructuring), Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), and applied progressive relaxation. Equal or superior to medication for long-term relapse prevention.

firstLine.rationale: Cleanest side-effect profile; start at 5mg for 7–10 days to minimize initial paradoxical jitteriness.
Broad-spectrum anxiolytic efficacy (covers comorbid panic, SAD, and OCD). Start low at 25mg.
SNRIs are first-line for GAD; especially beneficial when muscle tension and chronic somatic complaints are prominent.

secondLine.rationale: Non-controlled 5-HT1A partial agonist. Must be taken scheduled; zero risk of tolerance, dependence, or cognitive slowing.
Alpha-2-delta calcium channel ligand; rapid onset anxiolysis without typical serotonergic sexual side effects.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Non-addictive H1 antihistamine for acute breakthrough anxiety episodes without controlled-substance risks.
Dual serotonergic synergy augmenting partial SSRI responders.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Marked fear or anxiety about one or more social situations in which the individual is exposed to possible scrutiny by others, persisting >= 6 months.
ruleOuts: Avoidant personality disorder (pervasive self-concept of unworthiness vs social scrutiny)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: CBT with In-Vivo and Imaginal Exposure, Social Skills Training, and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). Exposure therapy is first-line gold standard.

firstLine.rationale: FDA-approved SSRIs with extensive clinical trials demonstrating reduction in social avoidance and autonomic blush/tremor.
High tolerability and broad anxiolytic efficacy across generalized social fears.

firstLine.agent: Propranolol (10–40mg PRN 30–60 min prior) — *Performance Only Specifier*
firstLine.rationale: Beta-blocker that blocks peripheral autonomic symptoms (tachycardia, diaphoresis, vocal tremor) during public speaking or musical performances without CNS sedation.

secondLine.rationale: Reserved for severe, disabling social paralysis while waiting for SSRI onset. High risk of dependence and blunting exposure therapy efficacy.
Documented efficacy in social anxiety with minimal drug interactions.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Combined medication + behavioral exposure prevents relapse upon eventual medication tapering.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Marked fear or anxiety about >= 2 of 5 situations: public transit, open spaces, enclosed places, lines/crowds, or being outside home alone, due to fear that escape might be difficult or help unavailable in the event of panic/incapacitation.
ruleOuts: Social anxiety disorder (fear of negative scrutiny rather than physical entrapment)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: In-Vivo Exposure Therapy (Graded Hierarchy) + CBT. Exposure to avoided real-world settings is the cornerstone of definitive recovery.

firstLine.rationale: Suppresses anticipatory dread and underlying panic surges, creating neurochemical stability required to engage in real-world exposure.
Proven efficacy in broad panic spectrum and agoraphobic avoidance. Start at low doses (e.g. Escitalopram 5mg) to avoid paradoxical activation.

secondLine.rationale: Potent tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) with pronounced serotonergic properties for SSRI-refractory panic/agoraphobia. Monitor ECG for QTc/conduction.
Alternative serotonergic switches if first trials fail.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: SSRI + High-Intensity Behavioral In-Vivo Exposure Coach
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Pharmacotherapy suppresses somatic panic while behavioral exposure extinguishes catastrophic safety behaviors.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Presence of obsessions (intrusive, unwanted thoughts/urges) and/or compulsions (repetitive mental or physical acts performed to neutralize anxiety), consuming >= 1 hour per day.
ruleOuts: Generalized anxiety disorder (worries about real-life concerns)
Depressive rumination (past failures vs future threat)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is the first-line psychotherapy of choice with the strongest empirical support. Compulsions must be systematically prevented during anxiety exposure.

firstLine.agent: High-Dose SSRIs: Fluoxetine (40–80mg), Sertraline (150–200+ mg), Fluvoxamine (150–300mg)
firstLine.rationale: OCD requires significantly HIGHER SSRI doses and LONGER trials (10–12 weeks at maximum tolerated dose) than major depression.
Proven antiobsessional efficacy; dosages above standard depression ranges often needed with ECG monitoring.

secondLine.rationale: Gold-standard TCA with unmatched serotonergic reuptake potency. Highly effective in severe refractory OCD; requires baseline ECG and seizure vigilance.

secondLine.agent: Class Switch to Alternative High-Dose SSRI
secondLine.rationale: Failure of one SSRI does not predict failure of another in OCD; try at least 2 distinct SSRIs before advancing.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: High-Dose SSRI + Low-Dose Atypical Antipsychotic (Aripiprazole 2–5mg, Risperidone 0.5–2mg, or Haloperidol)
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Dopamine D2 blockade synergizes with 5-HT reuptake inhibition to quiet basal ganglia hyperactivity in refractory OCD.
Attenuates hyperglutamatergic cortico-striatal-thalamo-cortical (CSTC) loop circuitry.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence; followed by >= 1 month of intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in mood/cognition, and marked hyperarousal (Criterion A–G).
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Trauma-Focused Psychotherapy: Prolonged Exposure (PE), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), or Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). Psychotherapy has larger effect sizes than medication alone.

firstLine.rationale: Only FDA-approved medications for PTSD. Broadly reduces hyperarousal, avoidance, and depressive intrusions.
First-line recommendation per VA/DoD and APA guidelines with robust clinical trial data.

secondLine.agent: Prazosin (Minipress 1–15mg at bedtime) — *Trauma Nightmares & Sleep Fragmentation*
secondLine.rationale: Centrally acting alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist. Dampens locus coeruleus noradrenergic hyperactivation, resolving trauma nightmares and insomnia. Titrate slowly to avoid orthostasis.
Enhances sleep continuity, reduces autonomic nightmares, and counteracts hyper-reactivity.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Multimodal standard of care: Stabilizes daytime hyperarousal, normalizes sleep, and processes traumatic memory networks.
Adjunctive suppression of refractory hypervigilance, paranoia, and severe dissociative flash-forwards.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor occurring within 3 months of the onset of the stressor, causing marked distress out of proportion and/or significant functional impairment; does not meet criteria for MDD or PTSD.
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: FIRST-LINE TREATMENT IS PSYCHOTHERAPY: Problem-solving therapy, crisis intervention, CBT, and stress management. Medication is NOT first-line and is strictly time-limited.

firstLine.agent: Short-Term Supportive Counseling / CBT & Sleep Hygiene
firstLine.rationale: Identifies adaptive coping strategies, processes situational transition (divorce, job loss, medical diagnosis), and prevents chronification.

firstLine.agent: Hydroxyzine (25–50mg PRN) or Trazodone (25–50mg QHS PRN) — *Short-Term Symptomatic Relief*
firstLine.rationale: Non-habit-forming, short-term relief of situational acute insomnia or daytime anxiety spikes. Avoid initiating chronic SSRIs or daily benzodiazepines.

secondLine.rationale: Indicated ONLY if symptoms fail to resolve after 4–8 weeks, if functional impairment escalates, or if the presentation evolves into a formal Major Depressive Episode.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Mindfulness Grounding + Social Work / Community Resource Connection
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Targets the tangible environmental or financial stressor driving the adjustment crisis.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Disruption of identity characterized by 2+ distinct personality states; recurrent gaps in recall of everyday events, personal info, and/or traumatic events; causes clinically significant distress.
ruleOuts: Borderline personality disorder (identity disturbance without amnesic barriers or separate executive states)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: GOLD STANDARD: Phase-Oriented Trauma Psychotherapy (ISSTD Guidelines). Phase 1: Safety, stabilization, grounding, and symptom reduction. Phase 2: Processing traumatic memories. Phase 3: Identity integration and rehabilitation. NO FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS EXIST FOR DID.

firstLine.rationale: Primary treatment is therapeutic, focused on internal communication, dialectical behavioral distress tolerance, and mapping alter states.
Treats secondary affective and trauma-related intrusive symptoms without disrupting internal system stability.

secondLine.rationale: Reduces severe nocturnal hyperarousal, night sweats, and dissociative night terrors.
Use cautiously for severe intrusive trauma-related auditory pseudohallucinations or overwhelming affective panic. (Avoid high doses that blunt cognitive processing).

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Strengthens distress tolerance, sensory grounding (TIPP skills), and self-soothing to eliminate self-harm and crisis hospitalizations.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Problematic pattern of alcohol use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, manifested by >= 2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria within a 12-month period.
ruleOuts: Primary major depressive or anxiety disorder masked by alcohol self-medication
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Motivational Interviewing (MI), CBT for relapse prevention, Twelve-Step Facilitation (AA), and Contingency Management.

firstLine.agent: Naltrexone (50mg PO daily or Vivitrol 380mg IM monthly)
firstLine.rationale: Mu-opioid receptor antagonist. Blocks dopamine surge associated with alcohol intake, extinguishing euphoria and reducing heavy drinking days. (Contraindicated in acute hepatitis or current opioid use).
Modulates NMDA and GABA receptors, dampening chronic alcohol withdrawal protracted dysphoria. Preferred in patients with hepatic impairment (renally cleared).

secondLine.rationale: Aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor producing toxic acetaldehyde accumulation if alcohol is consumed. Effective ONLY with supervised administration in highly motivated patients.

secondLine.agent: Topiramate (Topamax 100–300mg daily, off-label) or Gabapentin (900–1800mg daily, off-label)
secondLine.rationale: Facilitates GABAergic tone and inhibits glutamate; reduces cravings, improves sleep, and attenuates withdrawal anxiety.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Naltrexone (or Vivitrol) + Behavioral Relapse Prevention Therapy
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Synergistic reduction in craving and improved medication adherence.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Problematic pattern of cannabis use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, manifested by >= 2 of 11 criteria within 12 months.
ruleOuts: Cannabis Hyperemesis Syndrome (CHS - cyclical vomiting relieved by hot showers)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: FIRST-LINE TREATMENT IS PSYCHOTHERAPY: Motivational Enhancement Therapy (MET), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Contingency Management. No medications are currently FDA-approved for CUD.

firstLine.agent: Motivational Enhancement Therapy (MET) + CBT Coping Skills
firstLine.rationale: Resolves ambivalence, maps high-risk triggers, and develops alternative dopaminergic rewards and stress reduction.
Restores glutamate homeostasis in the nucleus accumbens. Shown in clinical trials to double abstinence odds and reduce cravings, particularly in adolescents and young adults.

secondLine.rationale: Significantly suppresses cannabis withdrawal symptoms (insomnia, vivid dreams, irritability, anorexia) during acute cessation.
Agonist replacement therapy off-label for severe withdrawal in inpatient or specialized addiction medicine contexts.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: NAC + Sleep Optimization (Trazodone / Melatonin) + Relapse Prevention
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Eliminates sleep disturbance as the primary trigger for cannabis relapse.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Recurrent behavioral outbursts representing failure to control aggressive impulses (verbal/physical aggression 2x/wk for 3 months, or 3 destructive/assaultive outbursts in 12 months); gross disproportion to provocation; chronologic age >= 6 years.
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Anger Regulation: Identifying somatic anger cues, cognitive restructuring of hostile attribution bias, relaxation skills, and structured time-outs.

firstLine.rationale: First-line pharmacotherapy: SSRIs enhance central serotonergic transmission, which is chronically hypoactive in impulsive aggression circuits (orbitofrontal cortex).

firstLine.agent: CBT Anger Management Protocol (Individual or Group)
firstLine.rationale: Teaches cognitive appraisal interruption before autonomic rage escalation occurs.

secondLine.rationale: Anticonvulsant mood stabilizers dampen central nervous system excitability and reduce frequency of violent outbursts.
Anti-aggressive and anti-impulsive properties well-documented in clinical trials.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: SSRI + Mood Stabilizer (Depakote or Lithium) + Second-Generation Antipsychotic (Risperidone 0.5–2mg)
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Triple modulation for severe, dangerous, refractory physical aggression.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts (A1–A3), accompanied by restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities (>= 2 of B1–B4); present in early development.
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), Social Skills Training, Speech/Language Therapy, Sensory Integration Occupational Therapy, and Parent Management Training. Core deficits do not respond to medications.

firstLine.agent: Aripiprazole (Abilify 2–15mg) or Risperidone (Risperdal 0.5–3mg) — *Targeting Severe Irritability & Agitation*
firstLine.rationale: The ONLY two FDA-approved medications for the treatment of severe irritability, physical aggression, tantrums, and self-injurious behavior associated with ASD.

firstLine.agent: Methylphenidate ER or Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) — *Targeting Comorbid ADHD Symptoms*
firstLine.rationale: Improves inattention and hyperactivity in up to 50% of ASD patients; titrate slowly due to increased sensitivity to behavioral side effects.

secondLine.rationale: Alpha-2A agonists improve hyperactivity, impulsivity, sensory over-reactivity, and sleep initiation.
Addresses comorbid anxiety, rigid repetitive compulsions, and transition meltdowns. Start at very low doses.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Minimizing auditory/visual overload dramatically enhances medication response.

pathways.conditionName: Cluster A Personality Disorders (Paranoid, Schizoid, Schizotypal)
pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Odd, eccentric personality configurations: Paranoid (SUSPECT - pervasive distrust/suspiciousness), Schizoid (DISTANT - detachment from social relationships, flat affect), Schizotypal (ME PECULIAR - magical thinking, ideas of reference, eccentric behavior).
ruleOuts: Schizophrenia (fixed unshakeable delusions, formal thought disorder, prominent hallucinations)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Supportive Psychotherapy: Maintain professional distance, respect autonomy, do not challenge suspiciousness directly, provide clear and transparent treatment rationale. (Avoid overly intrusive group therapies for schizoid/paranoid).

firstLine.rationale: Targeted reduction in transient cognitive-perceptual distortions, ideas of reference, and intense hyper-vigilant paranoia (especially in Schizotypal & Paranoid).
Consistency and predictable clinical scheduling without forcing intense intimacy.

secondLine.rationale: Attenuates secondary social anxiety and depressive demoralization.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Low-Dose SGA + Gentle CBT for Social Skills and Cognitive Flexibility
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Enhances day-to-day functional stability while avoiding institutional or adversarial conflict.

pathways.conditionName: Cluster B Personality Disorders (Borderline, Antisocial, Histrionic, Narcissistic)
pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Dramatic, emotional, erratic personality configurations: Borderline (I DESPAIRR - abandonment fears, unstable relationships/identity, suicidal/self-harm gestures, affective instability), Antisocial (CORRUPT), Histrionic (PRAISE ME), Narcissistic (SPEEECIAL).
ruleOuts: Bipolar II disorder (mood shifts in BPD are triggered by interpersonal stress and last hours, not weeks)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: FIRST-LINE TREATMENT IS SPECIALIZED PSYCHOTHERAPY: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT - gold standard for BPD), Mentalization-Based Therapy (MBT), or Schema Therapy. NO MEDICATIONS ARE FDA-APPROVED FOR PERSONALITY DISORDERS.

firstLine.agent: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT: Mindfulness, Distress Tolerance, Emotion Regulation, Interpersonal Effectiveness)
firstLine.rationale: First-line primary intervention. Significantly reduces suicide attempts, self-harm, ER visits, and hospitalizations.
Targeted off-label symptom relief for severe affective dysregulation, transient stress-induced paranoia, and impulsive anger.

secondLine.rationale: Shown in randomized trials to improve affective instability and reduce impulsive behavioral reactivity.
Evidence-supported adjunctive reduction in impulsive aggression and depressive symptoms in BPD.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: CRITICAL RULE: Benzodiazepines cause behavioral disinhibition, worsen impulsivity, and present lethal overdose risk with alcohol.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Comprehensive DBT + Clear Boundary Setting + Interdisciplinary Care Coordination
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Prevents institutional splitting and maintains safe, compassionate therapeutic containers.

pathways.conditionName: Cluster C Personality Disorders (Avoidant, Dependent, OCPD)
pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Anxious, fearful personality configurations: Avoidant (CRINGES - social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, hypersensitivity to negative evaluation), Dependent (RELIANCE - submissive, clinging behavior, fear of separation), Obsessive-Compulsive PD (LAW FIRMS - preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, mental/interpersonal control).
ruleOuts: Social anxiety disorder (overlaps heavily with Avoidant PD)
OCD (OCPD is egosyntonic; OCD is egodystonic with distressing obsessions/compulsions)
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Schema Therapy, and Graded Exposure Therapy. Helps patients build emotional tolerance for imperfection and autonomy.

firstLine.agent: CBT for Core Maladaptive Schemas (Defectiveness, Vulnerability, Perfectionism)
firstLine.rationale: Primary intervention targeting ingrained cognitive schemas and interpersonal avoidance.
Reduces underlying autonomic trait anxiety, rejection hypersensitivity, and secondary depressive demoralization.

secondLine.rationale: Addresses chronic perfectionistic somatic distress and severe anticipatory anxiety.
Anxiolytic adjunct to promote engagement in independence and exposure exercises.

augmentationStrategies.rationale: Dismantles safety behaviors and builds autonomous decision-making capacity.

pathways.diagnosticCriteriaSummary: Persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity interfering with functioning (>= 5 symptoms in adults), with origin prior to age 12.
ruleOuts: Severe primary anxiety/depression causing executive dysfunction
pathways.psychotherapyFirstOrAdjunct: ADHD-focused CBT, Executive Function Coaching, and Environmental Accommodations. Combined stimulant medication + behavioral coaching provides the highest functional outcome.

firstLine.rationale: Lysine-bound prodrug converted to active dextroamphetamine via red blood cell enzymes; provides 12–14 hour smooth coverage with lower abuse/diversion liability.

firstLine.agent: Mixed Amphetamine Salts XR (Adderall XR 10–30mg) or Methylphenidate ER (Concerta 18–72mg)
firstLine.rationale: First-line stimulants with extensive evidence base. Concerta's OROS delivery system ensures stable osmotic delivery.

secondLine.rationale: First-line non-controlled NRI option when patient has history of substance use disorder, severe anxiety, tic disorders, or cardiovascular contraindications.
Novel non-controlled multimodal NRI approved for adult ADHD. Monitor CYP1A2 interactions.
Dual noradrenergic/dopaminergic reuptake inhibition; ideal when adult ADHD co-occurs with Major Depression.

augmentationStrategies.strategy: Stimulant + Guanfacine ER (Intuniv 1–4mg) or Clonidine ER
augmentationStrategies.rationale: Alpha-2A agonist synergy strengthening prefrontal cortex networking, mitigating evening stimulant rebound, and managing rejection sensitive dysphoria.
